title: Chapter 1.  Geography — Location, Formation & Physical Features

blocks.content: Lakshadweep is India's smallest Union Territory and its only entirely coral-atoll archipelago — a geography chapter dominated by a handful of extremely specific, frequently tested superlatives (smallest UT, only coral-reef territory, fewest inhabited islands) rather than the sprawling mountain-range content of the Himalayan UTs.

Lakshadweep is a group of coral islands in the Arabian Sea, lying roughly 220 to 440 km off the Kerala coast (from the port city of Kochi), making it India's westernmost territory and its only island UT located in the Arabian Sea (in contrast to the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, which lie in the Bay of Bengal on the opposite side of the subcontinent).

The archipelago consists of 36 islands (some sources count slightly differing totals depending on how small islets and reefs are classified), of which only about 10 are inhabited, spread across a wider maritime area but with an extremely small total land area — making Lakshadweep by far India's smallest Union Territory (and smallest state/UT of any kind) by land area.

The islands are broadly grouped into three main coral formations: the Amindivi group (in the north, including Amini, Kadmat, Kiltan, Chetlat and Bitra), the Laccadive group (in the centre/south, including Kavaratti, Agatti, Andrott and Kalpeni), and the separate Minicoy island (the southernmost island, geographically and culturally closer to the Maldives than to the rest of Lakshadweep).

cells: approx 32 sq km — India's SMALLEST Union Territory/state by land area
36 (islands, islets and reefs); only about 10 inhabited
1 (the entire UT is a single district)
1 (Scheduled Tribe-reserved constituency, covering the entire UT) — one of India's smallest Lok Sabha constituencies by number of voters

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Lakshadweep is India's SMALLEST Union Territory by area (~32 sq km, smaller even than many individual city districts) — the single most repeated superlative fact about this UT, frequently paired in comparative questions with Ladakh as India's LARGEST UT by area.

Lakshadweep's islands are entirely coral in origin — low-lying coral atolls and reef platforms rising only a few metres above sea level, built up over geological time by the accumulated skeletal deposits of coral organisms, unlike the volcanic or continental-shelf origins of most other Indian islands (such as several Andaman & Nicobar islands).

This coral-atoll structure makes Lakshadweep India's only true coral-reef island territory, and gives the islands their characteristic lagoon-and-reef geography: each inhabited island typically has a shallow, turquoise lagoon on its western side (sheltered by the reef) and a more exposed, deeper-water eastern side facing the open sea.

Because of their low elevation (rarely exceeding a few metres above sea level), the islands are considered highly vulnerable to sea-level rise and coastal erosion linked to climate change — a significant and increasingly tested environmental theme (Chapter 8).

★ EXAM POINT: Lakshadweep is India's ONLY entirely coral-origin island territory — a key distinguishing fact from the volcanic/continental-shelf-origin islands of the Andaman & Nicobar group. This coral-vs-volcanic origin distinction is one of the most frequently tested geography comparison points between India's two island UTs.

cells: Tropical maritime/equatorial — warm, humid, with relatively little seasonal temperature variation given the moderating effect of the surrounding ocean
South-West monsoon (June-September) brings the bulk of annual rainfall; the islands are also affected by pre-monsoon and occasional cyclonic activity given their open-ocean exposure
Relatively narrow year-round, typically between roughly 22°C and 32°C, owing to the strong maritime moderating influence

items: Lakshadweep: approx 32 sq km — India's SMALLEST UT/state by land area; 36 islands, only ~10 inhabited.
Located in the Arabian Sea, ~220-440 km off Kochi, Kerala — India's westernmost, only Arabian Sea island territory.
Capital: Kavaratti; largest island: Andrott; single district for the whole UT; 1 Lok Sabha seat (ST-reserved).
Three groupings: Amindivi group (north), Laccadive group (centre/south), Minicoy (separate, southernmost, culturally close to the Maldives).
India's ONLY entirely coral-atoll island territory — distinct from the volcanic/continental-shelf-origin Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
